Why convert FIT to CSV for AI?

FIT is a compact binary activity format. CSV is text-based and easier for many analysis tools to inspect. FIT2CSV decodes the FIT file and places the available parser output into one CSV without adding its own coaching conclusions.

Keep detailed workout records

The full CSV can retain timestamped records and available fields such as heart rate, cadence, speed, power, altitude, GPS, laps, sessions, events, device information, and running dynamics when those values exist in the FIT file.

Let the analysis layer calculate metrics

The Full CSV remains a raw decoded export without coaching calculations. Separately, the optional Analyze with AI feature can create a compact workout summary for interpretation without changing the downloaded CSV.

Local conversion before sharing

The original FIT file is processed locally in the browser and is not uploaded. If you explicitly choose Analyze with AI, only compact workout metrics are sent to AI; filename, GPS coordinates and device serial number are excluded.

Frequently asked questions

Can an AI analyze the exported CSV?

Yes. Many AI and data-analysis workflows can work with CSV. The quality of the analysis depends on the fields available in the original FIT file and the capabilities of the analysis tool.

Does FIT2CSV provide AI workout analysis?

Yes, optionally. After a FIT file is decoded locally, you can choose Analyze with AI for a single-activity analysis. The Full CSV export remains unchanged and contains no AI-generated coaching fields.

Why keep record-level data?

Timestamped record data can allow downstream tools to examine how metrics such as heart rate, cadence, speed, power, and altitude change during the activity.

Is the FIT file sent to the AI service?

No. The original FIT file stays in your browser. If you choose AI analysis, FIT2CSV sends only a compact set of workout metrics to AI and excludes filename, GPS coordinates and device serial number.
